description: A structured onboarding journey for analysts supporting live game teams, business functions and data-driven decision-making.
roleMission: Turn reliable data into clear, timely insight that helps game teams make better decisions.
operatingModel: Build a deep understanding of the game, player journey, metrics and data landscape.
Partner with stakeholders to turn business questions into sound analytical work.
Deliver reusable analysis, documentation and a prioritized analytics roadmap.
journeyPrinciples: Understand the game, business model, data and existing analytical environment.
Explore player behavior, business performance and decision-making needs.
Deliver reliable analysis and one meaningful analytical improvement.
Partner through a sustainable stakeholder working model.

phaseSuccessCriteria.30: Critical access is available; the analyst understands the game, KPIs and player journey; main datasets, dashboards and stakeholders are mapped; a focused first analytical question is defined.
phaseSuccessCriteria.60: A meaningful analysis has been delivered; findings are credible and connected to decisions; one recurring workflow has been improved; stakeholders view the analyst as a reliable partner.
phaseSuccessCriteria.90: The analyst independently owns a defined analytical area; outputs are used by stakeholders; a credible six-month roadmap exists; strong data, communication and stakeholder practices are established.

suggestedResources: Data dictionaries, event taxonomy and pipelines
Existing queries, notebooks and analytical documentation

weeks.title: Foundation and access
weeks.focus: Become operational and understand the organizational and analytical environment.
outcomes: Required tools and data access are requested or completed
Initial understanding of the studio, game teams and analytics organization
Key recurring meetings and introductions are scheduled
Initial learning plan is established
activities: Secure access to SQL environments, dashboards, Looker, Jira, Confluence, Slack, GitHub and relevant data tools
Review the studio, portfolio and game-team structure
Understand Analytics ownership and review data dictionaries
Set weekly meetings with the manager and analytical lead

weeks.title: Game and business immersion
weeks.focus: Understand the game, player journey, business model and core KPIs.
outcomes: Initial understanding of the game loop and player lifecycle
Familiarity with key business and product KPIs
Understanding of how teams use data in decisions
activities: Play the game and document the core player journey
Join selected game, product and analytics meetings
Review DAU, MAU, retention, conversion, payer rate, ARPDAU, engagement and progression metrics
Review dashboards, reports, terminology and open questions

weeks.title: Data ecosystem and analytical workflows
weeks.focus: Learn where data comes from, how it is transformed and how analysis is delivered.
outcomes: Initial map of main datasets, events and dashboards
Understanding of recurring workflows and reporting needs
Awareness of data-quality or documentation gaps
activities: Review event taxonomy, major data tables and pipelines
Review queries, dashboards and analytical notebooks
Map recurring reporting and insight-generation workflows
Identify validation processes and data-quality issues

weeks.title: Stakeholder needs and decision mapping
weeks.focus: Understand how Product, Economy, Monetization and LiveOps make decisions.
outcomes: Key analytical customers and decision points are documented
Recurring analytical requests and pain points are identified
Initial analytical opportunity themes are captured
activities: Meet Product, Economy, Monetization, LiveOps and Production stakeholders
Document recurring business questions and decisions supported by Analytics
Identify manual reports, data-access pain points and current intake processes
Consolidate first-month findings

weeks.title: First-month synthesis
weeks.focus: Turn initial learning into a structured analytical map and development plan.
outcomes: Business and data understanding is summarized
Stakeholder map and opportunity backlog are established
One initial analysis is selected
activities: Summarize game, KPIs, datasets, dashboards and workflows
Create the stakeholder and analytical-demand map
Select a focused first analysis with the manager
Define the business question, scope and intended audience

weeks.title: First analytical deep dive
weeks.focus: Conduct a structured analysis of a meaningful business question.
outcomes: Analytical question and methodology are agreed
Relevant data is validated
Initial insights are produced
activities: Translate the business question into an analytical approach
Validate datasets and definitions
Build required SQL queries or analysis
Review assumptions and limitations with subject-matter experts

weeks.title: Insight generation and stakeholder feedback
weeks.focus: Turn analysis into clear, actionable insights.
outcomes: Findings are clear and supported by evidence
Stakeholder feedback is incorporated
Recommendations connect to business decisions
activities: Identify meaningful trends, segments, drivers and anomalies
Separate correlation from supported conclusions
Review findings with Product or business stakeholders
Refine the analysis and draft actionable recommendations

weeks.title: Reporting and workflow improvement
weeks.focus: Improve one recurring analytical or reporting workflow.
outcomes: A reporting or analytical pain point is selected
A proposed improvement is validated
Implementation scope is defined
activities: Identify one recurring manual report, query or dashboard workflow
Baseline current time, complexity and quality
Design a more efficient or reliable approach
Confirm ownership, dependencies and expected value

weeks.title: Deliver and document
weeks.focus: Deliver the first analytical output and establish reusable documentation.
outcomes: The first meaningful analysis is delivered
The workflow improvement is implemented or piloted
Documentation is available for future use
activities: Present the analysis and recommendations
Publish or update the dashboard, query or report
Document methodology, definitions and limitations
Capture stakeholder feedback and required follow-up

weeks.title: Independent analytical ownership
weeks.focus: Take ownership of a recurring analytical area or business problem.
outcomes: Clear analytical ownership is established
The analyst independently manages a defined scope
activities: Own a recurring analysis, dashboard or decision-support workflow
Establish a regular stakeholder cadence
Proactively identify relevant changes and anomalies
Improve communication of analytical findings

weeks.title: Measurement and impact
weeks.focus: Measure whether the first deliverables created value.
outcomes: Stakeholder usage and feedback are documented
Time, quality or decision-making improvements are assessed
activities: Measure adoption of the analysis or reporting improvement
Collect stakeholder feedback
Assess time saved, accuracy or decision impact
Identify required iterations

weeks.title: Analytical opportunity roadmap
weeks.focus: Build a prioritized backlog for the following six months.
outcomes: Analytical opportunities are prioritized
Dependencies and expected value are documented
activities: Consolidate outstanding analytical needs
Prioritize by impact, effort, urgency and data readiness
Identify dashboard, analysis, experimentation and data-quality opportunities
Align priorities with the manager and partners

weeks.title: Operating model and 90-day review
weeks.focus: Confirm role ownership, working rhythms and the path forward.
outcomes: Six-month analytical roadmap is agreed
Stakeholder working model is established
Development priorities are clear
activities: Present the prioritized analytical roadmap
Confirm recurring stakeholder and team cadences
Clarify intake, prioritization and delivery expectations
Complete reflections, manager assessment and skill-development priorities
